newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, Israel say need more time to restart peace.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, Israel say need more time to restart peace.

text.p: Egypt and Israel said at a Middle East peace summit on Tuesday they needed more time and consultations with the Palestinians to restart peace talks stalled by differences on Jewish settlements.

"We need another meeting and we need more deliberation," Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak told a news conference after three hours of talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh.

"I think you would agree that this is a positive beginning," Netanyahu said, referring to the meeting with Mubarak. "But we need more work and we are committed to work together with you (Egypt) to achieve progress."
Palestinian-Israeli peace talks have stopped since March when Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat refuses to restart talks until the construction work stops, something which Netanyahu has said he will not do. Egypt, which often mediates in peace talks, had said it would speak for the Palestinians at Tuesday's summit.
